genre: New Orleans party band — trad-jazz / 2nd-line / NOLA funk
artist_profile: The Hot Magnolias — Cincinnati 8-piece New Orleans party band (formed 2013; CCM players and scene vets). Repertoire runs 1920s trad-jazz standards through Mardi Gras 2nd-line to 70s NOLA funk. Live lineup: Jason Burkett (lead vocals), David Sharkey (sax), Chapman Sowash (trombone), Michael Cruse (trumpet), Kevin McClellan (bass), Jamarco Thomas (keys/piano), Bennett Kottler (banjo/guitar — one player doubling), Ryan Mitchell (drums/perc). The three-horn front line and the party energy ARE the show: mix horn-forward, warm and danceable — not a scooped rock sound.
research_summary: Band/lineup: Bandcamp, CincyMusic, NKyTribune. Per-source: A-T Pro 35 (A-T + Sweetwater + user reports — warmer than most clip-ons but slightly treble-forward, thin lows, 145 dB SPL, 80 Hz LC on the module); NOLA brass mixing (audiorecording.me — frequency-slot the three horns, watch upper-mid masking, keep overtones so they cut); banjo pickup DI (Banjo Hangout / BanjoTeacher — far more HF than a guitar pickup, plunky/zingy, needs top roll-off + body). KB eq-starting-points + mic-library for the drum kit, bass DI, SM57 overheads, Beta 58A.
room_context: Fountain Square open-air: no room gain, lows and HF dissipate over the throw, downtown noise floor + wind tighten gain-before-feedback. Support lows and presence, ease the deep low-mid cuts a room would need, cuts-first on everything, vocals cuts-only.
style_note: Horn-forward New Orleans party band — warm and danceable, three-horn front line carries the show.
changes: Kick / tom / snare low-mid cuts eased vs. a room build — FSQ open air has far less 250-400 Hz buildup, so mud cuts are lighter and low-end support is added instead.
Kick In (Beta 91A) carries the +3.5k attack; Kick Out (Audix D6) left near-flat — the D6 is pre-voiced (scooped mids, built-in click), so no stacked HF boost.
Overheads are on SM57s (dark dynamics for a loud open stage) — small +2 @ 10k air lift recovers cymbal sheen the 57 physically can't reach; a mic-limitation fix, not tone-shaping.
Hi-Hat is on a Sennheiser e609 (a cab dynamic) — unusual choice; EQ'd for its edgy 2.5-4k and its lack of top extension. FLAG: confirm e609 on hat vs. an SM81/SM57.
Horns (A-T Pro 35) get gentle top trims only — NOLA brass needs its overtones to cut, so the clip's plastic edge is eased without dulling the line; body added at 250-400 where the clip is thin.
Banjo DI top pulled hard at 4k — pickup zing is far brighter than a guitar; +2 @ 200 restores the body the pickup misses.
Vocal 1 / Vocal 2 written cuts-only with a DEQ on the Beta 58A 4k presence peak — this OVERRIDES the FSQ template's shipped vocal curve + feedback notch on faders 25/26. Confirm on the console.
reverb_note: Outdoor — reverb carries the space (no natural room). Keep pre-delay generous for intelligibility; a short plate on horns and lead vocal. Pull the specific Seventh Heaven Pro / Bricasti preset names from the KB reverb reference at the desk — not invented here.

channels.name: Kick In
channels.notes: Beta 91A/D6 two-mic kick — 91A is the attack/click layer inside on the batter head. Treat the pair as ONE: same VCA, pan together, blend constant. Polarity: sum in mono, flip one mic if thinner. Bus: notch -2/-3 @300-500 if it builds.
channels.mic_notes: Boundary on the batter head — the attack/click engine. Keep its lows tucked under the D6.
channels.eq_summary: +4 @ 3.5k gives beater definition that carries in open air; box (500) and mud (250) cuts eased because outdoor has far less low-mid buildup than a room; modest +3 @ 70 so it doesn't stack on the D6's voiced lows.

channels.name: Kick Out
channels.notes: Beta 91A/D6 two-mic kick — D6 is the body/thump core at the port. Treat the pair as one; pan together, same VCA.
channels.mic_notes: D6 is pre-scooped with a voiced ~4k click and big lows — it barely needs EQ; let it own the body.
channels.eq_summary: Almost flat by design — +3 @ 60 restores the weight open air eats, a small 400 nudge only if it builds. Top left alone: the D6's click is already voiced in and the 91A carries the real attack.

channels.name: Snare Top
channels.notes: Gate to reject hat/kick bleed without chopping ghost notes; release to tempo.
channels.mic_notes: i5 is punchy and mid-forward with its own 4-5k presence — ease the crack boost so it doesn't get spiky.
channels.eq_summary: Small +2 @ 5k for cut in open air (the i5 is already forward); 500 box cut for clarity; only a light 220 trim so the backbeat keeps its body — party-band snare wants pop and thump, not a thin rock crack.

channels.name: Hi-Hat
channels.notes: e609 on hat is unusual (it's a cab dynamic) — placement/rejection driven on a loud stage. Light ducker over a hard gate. FLAG mic choice.
channels.mic_notes: e609 is a flat-face cab dynamic — a hard ~4-5k presence, edgy 2.5-4k, and no airy top extension. It's here for rejection on a loud stage, not sheen.
channels.eq_summary: HPF hard at 500 to dump snare/kick bleed; tame the e609 edge at 3.5k and the 800 clank. No top boost — the mic doesn't reach there, and the overheads carry cymbal air. FLAG: confirm e609 vs. SM81/SM57 on the hat.

channels.name: Rack 1
channels.notes: Gate release matched to the kit's decay.
channels.mic_notes: D2 is voiced for mid toms — punchy with its own low-mid weight; mostly needs mud control.
channels.eq_summary: -3 @ 450 clears low-mid mud; +2 @ 110 restores body outdoors. Attack left alone — the D2 has its own punch and open air doesn't need extra stick.

channels.name: Floor
channels.notes: Gate release long enough to keep the floor's natural decay.
channels.mic_notes: D4 extends lower than the D2 — the floor's low-end owner.
channels.eq_summary: +3 @ 80 supports the boom open air swallows; -3 @ 400 keeps it from getting woofy. Top left natural.

channels.name: OH L
channels.notes: SM57 overheads — dark, bleed-rejecting for a loud open stage. Polarity check OH L vs OH R in mono; flip if the sum thins.
channels.mic_notes: SM57 as OH = deliberately dark and bleed-rejecting; it won't give natural cymbal sheen, hence the small air lift.
channels.eq_summary: +2 @ 10k gently restores the sizzle the 57 can't reach (like lifting a closed piano lid — a physical loss, not a mix choice); 3k honk and 400 box cut clean the cymbal wash. Polarity-check the pair in mono.

channels.name: OH R
channels.notes: Matched to OH L. Polarity check vs Ch 9 — sum in mono, flip if thinner.
channels.eq_summary: Matched to OH L — same dark-dynamic recovery curve. Polarity-check the pair in mono and flip one if the sum thins.

channels.name: Bass DI
channels.notes: Passive DI. Gentle comp to even note-to-note level.
channels.mic_notes: Whirlwind IMP passive DI — honest and flat, no active sparkle, so definition is an EQ job.
channels.eq_summary: +3 @ 80 anchors the low end open air eats; +2 @ 800 adds finger/growl definition that travels past the subs' throw for the dancers up front; 300 mud cut keeps it tight.

channels.name: Guitar
channels.notes: Bennett doubles banjo (Ch 15) and guitar — only one is live at a time. Single 57 (no ribbon blend outdoors).
channels.mic_notes: Mid-forward and proximity-prone — the cab box at 400 and the honk at 3k are the usual 57 suspects.
channels.eq_summary: -4 @ 400 kills the cab box; -2 @ 3k tames the 57 honk while leaving the upper presence so rhythm chank cuts. Sits under the horns — carve, don't feature.

channels.name: Banjo
channels.notes: Same player as Ch 13 — one live at a time. DI off the banjo pickup.
channels.mic_notes: DI off a banjo pickup — very bright and plunky, much more HF than a guitar pickup and thin on body.
channels.eq_summary: -4 @ 4k pulls the piezo/pickup zing that gets strident through a big PA; +2 @ 200 restores body the pickup can't; 800 plunk cut cleans the attack.

channels.name: Keys
channels.notes: Direct out via XLR. FLAG: confirm mono vs stereo (single fader assumed).
channels.mic_notes: Clean direct source — EQ is about carving space around bass/guitar/horns, not correcting a mic.
channels.eq_summary: -3 @ 300 opens room for the bass and low brass; -2 @ 3k softens any hard upper-mid from a digital piano/organ patch. Confirm mono vs stereo at patch.

channels.name: Sax
channels.notes: Clip-on; player moves (2nd-line). Fast-attack comp — brass transients jump.
channels.mic_notes: Pro 35 is warmer than most clip-ons but slightly treble-forward and thin down low; takes screaming SPL without complaint.
channels.eq_summary: Sax needs its upper harmonics to cut in a horn stack, so the top trim is gentle (-2 @ 6k, just the plastic edge); +2 @ 400 fills the body the clip loses; -3 @ 1k keeps the reed from barking.

channels.name: Trombone
channels.notes: Clip on the bell; player moves. Fast-attack comp.
channels.mic_notes: Low brass — its own weight at 200-300; the blat lives at 700-900. Pro 35 clip takes the bell SPL fine.
channels.eq_summary: +2 @ 250 keeps the bone warm and full; -3 @ 800 tames the blat; light -2 @ 5k off the clip's top. Kept musical — this is the fat middle of the horn line.

channels.name: Trumpet
channels.notes: Clip on the bell; player moves. Fast-attack comp.
channels.mic_notes: Brightest of the three horns; the blare zone is 2-4k when it's wailing. Pro 35 handles a lead trumpet at 4 inches without folding.
channels.eq_summary: -3 @ 2.5k tames the blare so the lead lines don't ice the ears through the A15s; light top trim off the clip. Left mostly open — the trumpet is the horn line's cutting edge and shouldn't be dulled.

channels.name: Vocal 1
channels.notes: Jason Burkett — lead. Cuts-only (feedback rule). Comp to even; expander opens on breath. OVERRIDES the FSQ template vocal curve on fader 25 — confirm on console.
channels.mic_notes: Beta 58A — brighter than an SM58 with TWO presence peaks (~4k and ~10k) and a tighter pattern for more gain before feedback on the open stage; those peaks can get strident.
channels.eq_summary: Cuts only. DEQ the 4k peak so it ducks only when he leans in; 600 box is the main feedback breeder outdoors; 250 proximity trim. Let the mic's own 10k air carry the top — no boosts.

channels.name: Vocal 2
channels.notes: Backing / shared (horn players sing gang vocals). Matched to Vocal 1. Mark SPARE if unused. Overrides template baseline on fader 26.
channels.eq_summary: Same cuts-only curve as Vocal 1. If it goes unused, pull it to SPARE; if a horn player is on it for shout choruses, it's ready.
